digest.component_or_area: check_raw_git_writes.py static gate / reconciler git adapter
propositions: The pre-R3 gate (R1/R2 mechanism rules) misses non-atomic tracker mutations composed from sanctioned git-adapter primitives outside the seam because it approves each call individually without enforcing protocol (atomic transaction wrapper).

R3 rule detects calls to git-adapter mutation primitives made from outside the reconciler write-seam modules by resolving receiver bindings (import form and dynamic-loader form per-file) and matching against the primitive set, firing only when receiver is a resolved git-adapter module reference.

R3 is disabled inside sanctioned seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py, _pass_lock_lifecycle.py) via explicit _SeamBindings.enabled flag; calling the primitives within those files is the atomic transaction and is not subject to the composition rule.

Out-of-seam R3 hits are sanctioned by reusing the existing '# raw-git-ok: reason' inline marker (function-level or line-level, reason mandatory); two enumerated sites carry durable reasoned markers for non-remediable concurrency-safe patterns (binding-snapshot selective-commit boundary and detached-index CAS lock purge).

First-run dry-enumeration found exactly 7 R3 hits across 2 functions with zero false positives across src/ and scripts/, confirming receiver binding yields no false positives on non-git-adapter .add/.commit calls or read-only exports.

Implementation split __main__.py's pass-lock lifecycle into _pass_lock_lifecycle.py to stay under module-size gate while preserving all R3 markers with their durable reasons; R3 applies to the new file as a non-seam module.
